The German data are updated automatically every month from the [Energy-Charts API](https://api.energy-charts.info/) of Fraunhofer ISE. There is no public API for China; the annual values come from the statistical communiqués of the National Bureau of Statistics and are added after each new release (end of February) — with the original link for every value.

## Germany: installed capacity and target path

Solid lines show installed capacity, dashed lines and circles the statutory target path (EEG 2023 for onshore wind and solar PV; for offshore wind the WindSeeG only sets a 2030 target), as reported by Energy-Charts. Solar PV as module capacity (DC). The current-year value is provisional.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
chartLeistung
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`<span class="legende-art">━ installed &nbsp; ╍ target path &nbsp; ○ target value</span>

**Installed ${letzteIst[0].jahr} (provisional):** ${letzteIst.map(d => `${d.name} ${fmt1(d.gw)} GW`).join(" · ")}<br>
**2030 targets:** ${ziel2030.map(d => `${d.name} ${fmt0(d.gw)} GW`).join(" · ")}`
```

## Germany: monthly electricity generation from wind and sun

Public net electricity generation in TWh per month (excluding industrial self-supply), calculated from 15-minute values.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false

```

## Germany and China: installed capacity compared

Year-end values 2015–2025. **China:** statistical communiqués of the National Bureau of Statistics (国家统计局), in each case the first publication in the following year. **Germany:** Energy-Charts, wind = onshore + offshore, solar PV as module capacity (DC). Both in GW, same scale per technology.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
chartVergleich
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
tabelleKennzahlen
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`**Electricity generation 2025:** China — wind ${fmt0(cnErz.Wind)} TWh, solar ${fmt0(cnErz.Photovoltaik)} TWh (statistical communiqué, energy production table). Germany — wind ${fmt0(deErz.wind)} TWh, solar ${fmt0(deErz.pv)} TWh (public net generation, Energy-Charts).`
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Points to note when comparing

- **First publication:** The statistics bureau publishes preliminary values. Later revisions only appear in subsequent years; this series deliberately uses the first published value, so that each value maps to exactly one source. Growth rates stated in the communiqué may therefore differ from the difference between two annual values.
- **Definitions:** Up to 2024 the communiqué refers to "grid-connected" (并网) capacity, in 2025 without this qualifier. The source does not state whether solar PV is reported as DC or AC capacity. The values are therefore comparable in order of magnitude, not to the decimal place.
- **Generation:** Chinese generation values come from the energy production table; German values cover only public net generation, excluding industrial self-supply.
- **Excluding Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan** (according to the source).
:::

## Data sources

| Country | Source | Type | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| DE | Fraunhofer ISE – Energy-Charts | scientific, API, CC BY 4.0 | **live** |
| DE | Federal Network Agency – SMARD | official, cross-check | planned |
| DE | AGEE-Stat / German Environment Agency | official, annual values incl. geothermal heat | planned |
| CN | National Bureau of Statistics (国家统计局) – statistical communiqué | official, annual values, maintained manually | **live** |
| CN | National Energy Administration (国家能源局, NEA) | official, monthly releases | planned |
| both | Ember | secondary source, for cross-checking only | planned |

## Methodological notes

- **Different update frequencies:** For Germany 15-minute values are available; for China mainly annual and monthly values are publicly accessible. The country comparison is therefore on an annual basis.
- **Definitions:** "Public net generation" as defined by Energy-Charts excludes industrial self-supply. For China, the source's definitions are documented for each value.
- **Revisions:** The last three months are recalculated at every update; older months stay unchanged and can be traced in the repository's version history.
- **Code:** [scripts/fetch_energy_charts.py](https://github.com/jinggling09/jinggling09.github.io/blob/main/scripts/fetch_energy_charts.py)
